scope_description.value: Replacement of an existing deteriorated wooden retaining wall at the east side of the Hall A berm at Jefferson Lab with a new concrete cantilevered retaining wall. The wall protects an existing exhaust vent and critical utility systems. A temporary gravel access road off CEBAF Blvd is required for equipment access. After construction, the access road will be filled and restored to original grade and hydraulic capacity. Total disturbance area approximately 0.64 acres.
scope_description.quote: This report presents a comprehensive analysis of a multidisciplinary design involving the replacement of an existing wooden retaining wall protecting an existing exhaust vent. The project will entail the construction of a proposed concrete retaining wall. A temporary gravel access road will be constructed to facilitate equipment to access the existing wooden retaining wall.

corroboration.claim: replacement of an existing wooden retaining wall protecting an existing exhaust vent ... construction of a proposed concrete retaining wall

structural_design_parameters.quote: The foundation for the retaining wall will be a continuous reinforced spread footing with a thickness of 12 inches and width of 6 feet. The retaining wall will be a 12-inch-wide reinforced concrete wall system. A drain board with corrugated pipe will be placed on the back face (soil side) of the retaining wall to minimize water pressure on the wall.

conflict_flags.rationale: The RFP figure ($150K–$250K) was the pre-design budget estimate provided at solicitation (August 2023). The BOD figure ($314,200) is the engineer's opinion of probable construction cost at final design completion (February 2024). The BOD value is later, more detailed, and represents the final design position. Both values are preserved in separate fields. The cost growth from budget to final estimate (~26–110% over the upper/lower bounds) is significant and worth flagging for proposal use.
